Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the redline. I reviewed Acceleon_MSA_redlines_v3.docx and drafted two short options for each bucket (see notes below). I attached a text file with the exact snippets (Redwood_proposed_snippets.txt) to speed inline redlines if you want to push them back. Key points:

1) Output ownership
- Option A (Customer assignment): "Subject to Customer’s payment of all fees due hereunder, Contractor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to Customer-specific Outputs (excluding Contractor’s pre-existing models and model weights). Customer may use, reproduce, modify, and distribute such Outputs without restriction." — Pros: aligns with their ask. Cons: requires carveouts to prevent assignment of Redwood underlying models.
- Option B (License + Sublicense carveout): "Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and modify Customer-specific Outputs; Contractor retains all underlying model IP and any generalizable improvements." — Pros: protects Redwood model IP; may be acceptable operationally.

2) Training/data use
- Suggested language: "Contractor will not use Customer Content to improve or retrain Contractor models without Customer’s prior written opt-in. Customer may opt-in on a per-project or account-wide basis as set forth in the Order Form." — this meets their opt-in ask; requires contract tagging and internal ops to track opted-in accounts.

3) Feedback license
- Narrow approach: "Customer grants Contractor a non-exclusive, limited, revocable license to use aggregated feedback for model improvements, provided such use does not include Customer Content or personally identifiable data."
- Broad approach (they requested perpetual R-F): "Customer grants Contractor a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Feedback in connection with the development and improvement of Contractor’s products and models, provided that Contractor will not disclose Customer Confidential Information." — broad approach is customer-favorable; we can accept in exchange for a commercial concession.

Operational notes:
- If we accept assignment of Outputs, Procurement will likely request indemnities/escrow and activation of additional telemetry/evidence for lineage.
- We need to coordinate with Product to implement an opt-in flag in provisioning and to ensure audit logs for accounts that opt into training.
- Recommend a short JML (just-in-time) playbook for CS/PS handoff if they opt-in to retraining.

Next steps: Jordan, I can draft tracked-change redlines for the MSA/Order Form. Karthik — can you confirm whether Procurement terms (billing/SLA) need changes if we accept Option A vs B?

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
